chapter_seo_title: Chapter 528 – The Prince of Ren’s Mansion: Li Huowang’s Spine-Sword Discovery
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang tests the spine-sword’s hidden power: it can send people alive to Great Qi. A game-changing discovery for his plan to counter the Dice. But first, a prince’s opera and a naked performer.
og_title: Li Huowang Discovers the Spine-Sword’s True Power
og_description: A new strategy to counter the Dice emerges as Li Huowang learns he can transport people—and maybe himself—to Great Qi alive. Meanwhile, the Prince of Ren’s mansion hides darker entertainment.
twitter_title: Li Huowang just found out the spine-sword can *send* people to Great Qi. Alive. This changes everything.
twitter_description: The plan against the Dice just got teeth. Li Huowang tests the spine-sword’s transport function on a eunuch sentry—then discovers a naked, painted opera singer in the Prince of Ren’s bedchamber.

lore_anchors.definition: A prince of Great Liang, the emperor’s second brother, whose title means “Benevolent Prince.” He is Ji Lin’s rival for the throne and is rumored to employ rogue cultivators.
Li Huowang’s weapon, crafted from a segment of a Qi dynasty spine. It can cut into Great Qi’s history, previously used to kill, and now discovered to also be able to transport living beings there.
The past dynasty from which Zhuge Yuan originates; a separate historical layer that Li Huowang can access through the spine-sword’s slashes.
A general term for female roles in traditional Chinese opera. In this chapter, the performer wears full stage makeup but is completely naked, creating a jarringly obscene image.
In traditional Chinese timekeeping, the second of five night watches, roughly 9:00–11:00 PM.
An imperial robe embroidered with dragon patterns, worn by the emperor and direct princes of the blood as a symbol of status.
A cultivator who practices forbidden, heterodox arts outside the bounds of traditional Daoist or Buddhist cultivation, often associated with murder and black magic.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What did Li Huowang discover about the spine-sword?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He discovered that it can send people alive to Great Qi, not just kill them. This opens up a tactical option to use it as a transport mechanism, potentially even for himself.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn’t Li Huowang go to Great Qi immediately?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He restrains himself because he needs to finish the assassination of the Prince of Ren first. He still requires Ji Lin’s political support to counter the Dice, and he can’t afford to neglect either goal.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the Prince of Ren?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is the second brother of the late emperor of Great Liang, Ji Lin’s older brother. He is a contender for the throne and is rumored to employ rogue cultivators, including the one who killed Ji Lin’s mother and sister.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is so disturbing about the opera performer in the bedchamber?
cultural_notes_faq.a: She is wearing full stage makeup as a female role (dan), but her body is completely naked. The combination of formal art and raw, vulnerable exposure is intentionally grotesque and suggests a power dynamic of total control.
